product: Miracle-Gro Water Soluble Bloom Booster (10-52-10, high-phosphorus 'lavender' formula)
rate: In-ground beds: 4 tbsp powder dissolved in 16 oz warm water in the hose-end sprayer jar, dial set to 1 tbsp (0.5 oz); sprays roughly 4 gallons of finished mix over a 64 sq ft (8x8 ft) bed in 30-45 seconds. Established roses in-ground can take 2 tbsp per 2 gallons poured around the drip line. Potted plants: switch to a watering can at 1 tbsp powder per 1 gallon of water, poured directly onto the soil (never sprayed over foliage/blooms in pots - too easy to overdose a small volume of soil).
timing: Snip spent seed pods/flowers first so nutrients go straight to new bud production, then apply. In-ground/bed use: once every 4-6 weeks through summer, always after a plain-water soak of dry soil first. Potted heavy feeders (tropicals like Cuphea, Golden Shrimp Plant): every 2 weeks. Potted moderate feeders (Agastache, Black-eyed Susan, Blue Daze): every 3-4 weeks. Potted lean-soil natives (Gaillardia, Coneflower): once every 6 weeks max - overfeeding causes weak, floppy stems in prairie-adapted species.
notes: High phosphorus (52 middle number) signals roots to stop pushing leaf growth and start forming flower buds - expect tight green buds within 4-7 days and a full bloom flush by day 10. Continuous overuse builds up phosphorus that locks up iron/zinc, causing chlorosis (yellowing) - use as a temporary bloom kick-starter, not a everyday feed. Never spray directly onto open flowers/petals visited by pollinators; apply to soil in the evening after pollinator activity has stopped so it fully absorbs before bees/hummingbirds return. Do not use on plants being grown specifically for seed harvest - high phosphorus can reduce seed viability/germination; use a slow-release organic granular feed (e.g., Jobe's Organics) on seed-mother plants instead.
